lessons.expl:
·אמר רב זביד משמיה…QuestionWestwood int. · Jan 30, 2013 · 22:02
① The Gemara said above that the dispute between:
Ⓐ Rabbah
Ⓑ and Rava
② is really the same dispute as that of:
Ⓐ the Tanna Kamma (Rabbi Meir)
Ⓑ and Rabbi Yehuda
③ And although there is more than one possible way to explain the point over which they are disputing, it was originally thought that the Tanna Kamma and Rabbi Yehuda hold as follows:
Ⅰ A sign that could have come by itself:
Everyone agrees it is a good sign.
Ⅱ Passing by food:
Everyone agrees you can pass by food.
Ⅲ A sign that is usual to be trampled:
Ⓐ
It is not a good sign.
Ⓑ Rabbi Yehuda:
It is a good sign, it is a sign.
④ Rav Zvid, in the name of Rava, now asks:
According to this explanation, the Tanna Kamma holds:
Ⓐ You can pass by food.
Ⓑ A sign that is usual to be trampled is not a good sign.
⑤ And that is why the Tanna Kamma (Rabbi Meir) holds you may keep the fig cakes with the pottery shard inside and the loaf of the baker with the money inside.
⑥ The Tanna Kamma himself stated above in the Mishnah that he holds that if a person finds loaves of a private person, even in a public place, you must announce it.
⑦ If it is true, like the Amoraim originally thought, regarding their explanation of the Tanna Kamma, as to why he holds you must announce loaves of a private person found in a public place…

Ⓐ Rava, with a V.
Ⓑ And Rabbah, with a B.
Can explain the Mishnah according to their reasoning.
② Rava:
Ⓐ The dispute between the Tanna Kama/Rabbi Yehuda by the case of the Parshas can be explained that they are arguing whether or not a sign that could come by itself is a good sign.
Ⅰ Tanna Kama:
it is not a sign.
Ⅱ Rabbi Yehuda:
it is a sign.
Ⓑ Both the Tanna Kama and Rabbi Yehuda hold:
A sign that is usual to be trampled is a sign.
Ⓒ Both hold you can pass by food.
Ⓓ So it comes out:
Rabbi Yehuda holds: You must announce the loaf with the money inside. Since it is a sign and since a sign that will be trampled is a good sign.
Ⓔ The Tanna Kama holds:
You may keep the loaf with the money inside. Since it has no sign. Because he holds that a sign that could come by itself is not a sign.
In a public place, you must announce them, since they have an intrinsic sign and the owner is an optimist.
③ Rabbah:
Ⓐ The dispute between the Tanna Kama and Rabbi Yehuda by the loaf with money inside is whether or not a sign that could come by itself is a sign.
Ⅰ Tanna Kama:
it is not a sign.
Ⅱ Rabbi Yehuda:
it is a sign.
Ⓑ Both the Tanna Kama and Rabbi Yehuda agree:
a sign that is usual to be trampled is not a sign.
Ⓒ Both hold you cannot pass by food.
Ⓓ So it comes out that Rabbi Yehuda holds:
you must announce the loaf with the money inside. Since it is a good sign and it will not get trampled because you cannot pass by food.
Ⓔ The Tanna Kama holds:
you may keep the loaf with the money inside. Since a sign that could come by itself is not a good sign.
Ⓕ However, by loaves of a private person in a public place, the finder must announce them. Since such loaves have an intrinsic sign and it will not get trampled since you cannot pass by food.
